headline: HIGH-GRADE AT DEPTH: Aya Gold Drills 2,176 g/t Ag Over 8.4m at Zgounder's Pit Floor
snippet: Aya Gold & Silver reported pit-depth drill results at Morocco's Zgounder Silver Mine, with hole T28-26-1248 returning 2,176 g/t silver over 8.4m including 4,298 g/t over 3.6m. Results confirm strong mineralization continuity; 9,250m — 30.8% of the 2026 program — has been drilled to date.

headline: WYOMING URANIUM DOUBLES: Six Mines Now Running as Federal Billions Target US Supply Chain
snippet: Wyoming now hosts six uranium mines in operation — double the 2021 count — as the federal government pours billions into rebuilding domestic uranium supply. Industry says prices need to hold above $100/lb to sustain the revival; uranium currently trades around $85/lb.

headline: GOLD CLIMBS BACK to $4,502 as US-Iran Ceasefire Deadlock Keeps Safe-Haven Bid Alive
snippet: Gold recovered above $4,500/oz on June 2, up $54 from the prior session, with ongoing US-Iran peace negotiation deadlock and Federal Reserve rate-hike expectations driving safe-haven demand. Gold is up roughly $1,158 year-over-year as inflation and Middle East tensions keep the bid elevated.

headline: BANK OF AMERICA Lifts 2026 Gold Price Target to $5,000 Per Ounce
snippet: Bank of America revised its 2026 gold price forecast to $5,000/oz as institutional confidence in the precious metals rally solidifies. Gold miners are generating record free cash flow with all-in sustaining costs still below $2,000/oz, creating exceptional leverage to spot prices near all-time highs.

headline: SPROTT'S McINTYRE: Fed Trapped Between Inflation and Debt Crisis — Gold Wins Either Way
snippet: Sprott Inc. president Ryan McIntyre argues the Federal Reserve has no good options: keeping rates high risks a slowdown; cutting them risks losing control of inflation. In either scenario, confidence in sovereign debt erodes — and all roads lead to gold, he says.

headline: GOLD FLOWS EAST: Hong Kong Surpasses Switzerland as World's Top Cross-Border Gold Hub
snippet: Hong Kong has overtaken Switzerland as the world's largest cross-border wealth hub, per BCG's 2026 Global Wealth Report, driven by its push into gold trading. A new government-backed clearing system mirroring LBMA infrastructure launches in July; storage capacity is targeting a 10x expansion to 2,000 tonnes.

headline: 1,811 g/t SILVER: Brixton Metals Hits Ultra-High Grade at Ontario's Historic Cobalt Camp
snippet: Brixton Metals (TSXV: BBB) drilled 2.3m grading 1,811 g/t silver within a broader 27.7m interval at 166.45 g/t at its Langis Silver Project in Ontario's Cobalt camp. The 2026 campaign — 60,000m and the largest in project history — has now completed 14,760m across 72 holes.

headline: PAN AMERICAN SILVER Commits $146M to Deepen Timmins Camp as Bell Creek Drilling Finds New Ore Shoots
snippet: Pan American Silver will invest approximately $146 million at its Timmins, Ontario operations, including a 625m Bell Creek shaft extension and new access drifts to the Vogel and Samson deposits. The company plans 118,000m of drilling at Timmins in 2026, with updated mineral resources due in Q3.

headline: COPPER HITS $6.56/lb as Chile Reports Weakest Output in 23 Years and China Acid Supply Dries Up
snippet: Copper climbed to $6.56 per pound on June 2 — up 35.7% year-over-year — as Chile reported its weakest April output in 23 years and Chinese sulfuric acid exports to Chilean mines ceased completely. The dual supply shock of ore grade decline plus processing acid shortage has no quick fix, and AI data center and energy transition demand continues to underpin copper prices.

headline: LITHIUM DOUBLES IN MONTHS to $24,086/t as Energy Storage Boom Drives Junior Stock Revival
snippet: Battery-grade lithium carbonate has surged to approximately $24,086 per metric ton in 2026, nearly doubling in under two months as energy storage demand jumped 71% in 2025 and is forecast to grow another 55% this year. Australian producers Mineral Resources and Core Lithium restarted mothballed mines, helping lift junior lithium stocks.
